provenance.description: Omarchy desktop sounds for window, workspace, volume, power, and notification events. Includes per-event sound selection, six bundled sound packs, mute, relative volume, previews, and conservative DND, lock, and idle safety gates.
provenance.referenceImplementation: Omarchy shell plugin conventions and gobijan.ui-sounds desktop-event filters; no notification implementation retained.

runtime: pipewire-audio (pw-play)
sound-theme-freedesktop: device-added.oga, device-removed.oga, audio-volume-change.oga, power-plug.oga, power-unplug.oga (stereo)
python-dbus (observer child; installed 1.4.0-2)
python-gobject (observer child; installed 3.56.3-1)

panel.lifecycle: First-party on-demand panel pattern: the plugin declares both service and panel entry points (keepLoaded remains true), and the shell panel loader injects the already loaded live service into the panel.
panel.integration: Service.qml exposes `readonly property alias controllerApi: controller`; the panel reads and writes that single live controller slice and never creates a second ChimeController, settings store, player, or notification observer. No optimistic duplicate UI state: controls bind to the controller's reactive properties and invoke its existing setters (enabled/setEnabled, volume/setVolume, desktopEnabled/setDesktopEnabled, notificationsEnabled/setNotificationsEnabled), persisting through the existing schema-v4 store; writes are disabled until settingsReady. Each event row displays a human-readable label while retaining its camelCase settings/IPC id (issue #9). Choosing a sound calls controllerApi.preview(eventName) once after a successful assignment; issue #8 removes the separate preview-button section. Diagnostics read the service's safetyReason and overlapReason() plus controller status; they expose no notification contents or raw telemetry.
panel.invocation: Summoned and closed entirely through the shell panel host: `omarchy-shell shell summon omarchychime.sounds '{}'`, `omarchy-shell shell hide omarchychime.sounds`, `omarchy-shell shell toggle omarchychime.sounds '{}'`; user-initiated close routes through shell.hide("omarchychime.sounds"). The chime IPC target remains authoritative and includes pack/packs commands alongside per-event sound commands.
panel.scope: Exposes master sounds, Chime relative volume 0-1, desktop sounds, notification sounds, one whole-theme dropdown, and one sound dropdown per event. Theme selection replaces all eight assignments atomically; a subsequent event edit derives Custom state. Choosing a theme previews its notification cue; choosing an event sound previews that cue. Omarchy remains the notification owner.

barWidget.pattern: First-party bar-widget conventions (omarchy.menu icon + omarchy.media service+bar-widget pairing): BarWidget root, WidgetButton with a Nerd Font bell glyph, bar-injected shell/host access.
barWidget.integration: Reaches the one live controller through the shell host: bar.shell.firstPartyServiceFor("omarchychime.sounds").controllerApi. Left click runs `omarchy-shell shell toggle omarchychime.sounds '{}'` (the existing on-demand settings panel, no second UI); right click calls controllerApi.setEnabled(!enabled) — the compact mute control deferred from issue #4; wheel steps volume ±5% clamped to 0-1 via setVolume. The glyph is bell-ring (enabled) or bell-off (muted), dimmed while settings are loading. No second controller/store/player/observer and no new IPC verbs.
barWidget.placement: User-controlled placement only: manifest declares barWidget.defaultSection right; enabling (`omarchy plugin enable omarchychime.sounds`) inserts the layout entry there and `omarchy bar move omarchychime.sounds --section left|center|right` relocates it. The plugin never edits shell.json bar layout or other widgets.
barWidget.verification: Live on 2026-09-12: widget registered (debugBarGeometry slot itemVisible), bell-ring glyph rendered on the bar and swapped to dimmed bell-off on `chime mute` (screenshot-confirmed), unmute restored bell-ring; panel summon/hide/toggle round trips via the shared host still pass with the bar-widget kind present; `omarchy plugin validate .`, strict qmllint (all product QML/JS + tests/service-safety.qml with the installed host's qs mapping), 44 Node and 35 Python tests green. Note: bar-widget QML edits require a normal shell restart to take effect (registry re-registers the same component on hot reload; Qt's qmlcache also served stale bytecode until cleared).

integrationFields.safetyReady: conservative valid DND/lock/idle state + unlocked/nonidle/nonDND + real screen + settled startup; prefers legacy direct host services, with strict fail-closed Omarchy 4.0.3 fallbacks through persisted notification DND state and public lock/idle IPC
integrationFields.overlapBlocked: pluginRegistry.isEnabled('gobijan.ui-sounds') === true; unknown registry or unknown state => blocked
integrationFields.systemReady: SystemEvents.ready passed through; OR of volumeReady (default PipeWire sink baseline) and powerReady (UPower on-battery baseline); a missing backend keeps that source unready
integrationFields.observerActive: safetyReady && controller.settingsReady && controller.enabled && controller.notificationsEnabled; independent of desktop activation, ui-sounds overlap, and desktop adapter readiness
integrationFields.soundSelection: Every event's cue is a catalog sound id in the v4 settings sounds map. setThemePack atomically replaces the complete map with System default, Zen Wood, Ceramic Drop, Kalimba, Deep Resonance, Sonar, or Retro Hacker assignments; exact matching derives the selected pack and any per-event edit derives Custom. setEventSound validates and persists individual overrides. The panel exposes both selectors and previews successful choices.

agent-needs-input.wav.format: RIFF/WAVE, PCM 16-bit mono 44100 Hz, 0.385 s, peak 0.3
agent-needs-input.wav.synthesis: Original one-off eval synthesis: two sine tones E5 then A5 (~659.255 Hz then ~880 Hz), 170 ms each, 45 ms raised-cosine fades, 45 ms gap, peak 0.3. No embedded metadata. Project license: MIT (see license below).

mappings.powerConnected: device-added.oga (theme default power-plug.oga is a symlink)
mappings.powerDisconnected: device-removed.oga (theme default power-unplug.oga is a symlink)

freedesktop theme assets.catalog: issue #7: the 18 distinct theme .oga files after symlink canonicalization (power-plug, power-unplug, dialog-error, window-attention, window-question, screen-capture, network-connectivity-* excluded as symlink aliases; audio-channel-*, audio-test-signal excluded as calibration tones) plus the one local plugin asset, exposed as SOUND_CATALOG in ChimeLogic.js
freedesktop theme assets.note: Stock sound-theme-freedesktop files provided by the host desktop, not shipped by this plugin; the notification cue is the only local asset. The asset file and provenance are kept from alpha 2 (originally the agent-needs-input cue); only its semantic role changed — it now cues every newly accepted non-suppressed notification via notificationReceived.

bundled theme packs.format: 48 RIFF/WAVE files, PCM 16-bit mono 44100 Hz; one cue per pack for each of the eight events
bundled theme packs.catalog: Each bundled cue has a stable <pack>:<event> id in SOUND_CATALOG and a plugin-relative path resolved by ChimeController. Each pack directory carries its own source and mastering provenance in manifest.json.

currentRelease.issue2Race: Automatic desktop and power cues remain exempt from post-exit cooldown and use latest-only preemption. Rapid volumeUp/volumeDown events also ignore cooldown after completion, but coalesce while a volume cue is still playing so tonal WAVs reach their zero-valued tail instead of being terminated mid-wave. Notification cues and previews retain cooldown.

verification.limitations: Physical power plug/unplug and audible power-cue verification have not been performed. Physical multi-monitor audibility has deterministic coverage only. Lock and idle transitions were simulated in the isolated QML harness rather than by physically locking the session. Notification replacement ambiguity fails closed by design: genuine updates never re-cue, and an ambiguous equal-ID reply may stay silent.
